sweep.prompts:
A beautiful stained glass window in the style of safarieyes, made of small flat color panels. Each panel is fully just one color, but they are so small and there's so much of them that the image is very detailed. It depicts a desert scenery with rolling sand dunes and a lush oasis. The sun is setting in the horizon. Next to the oasis is a busy space port with a sleek, futuristic ship just about to take off. The work behind the flat color panels and the intricate details have clearly required a great deal of artistry and skill
inkpoet, midjourney, PaperDaal, whimsical storybook illustration, Overhead cinematic still of a 20-year-old woman passed out drunk in tall summer grass, lying on her back on a rumpled picnic blanket, mouth wide open mid-snore, slack jaw, messy hair stuck to her face, one arm thrown out. A tiny black kitten sprawled on her chest in an absurd drunken pose, belly up, one paw on her cheek, head lolling, eyes half-shut. An empty wine bottle on its side in the grass. The picnic is wrecked: torn baguette, smeared cheese, olive pits, crumpled napkins, a bitten peach browning in the sun. Her smartphone lies in the grass, screen on, large text reading Weekend. Late afternoon park light, warm and a bit cruel, crumbs and grass blades in sharp focus, photoreal 35mm film, fine grain, shallow depth of field, comedy of collapse
A sunlit cinematic scene of a young woman taking a lunch break at a bustling local roadside food stall. Her vintage moped is parked nearby, with her retro helmet with cat ear decoration resting on the seat. She is sitting on a simple stool in front of the stall, holding a bowl of steaming noodles, eating while looking around curiously at the surrounding landscape. She wears blue loose casual overalls with rolled cuffs, simple sneakers, and a canvas backpack slung over her shoulders. Warm daytime sunlight, soft shadows, steam rising from the bowl, low saturation color grading, painterly photorealism with fine texture detail on fabric, food, and metal. Subtle film grain, 35mm feel, realistic lighting, relaxed and curious mood

sweep.prompts:
An old photographer's darkroom occupies the back of a 1950s studio, its walls lined with enamel developing trays, steel sinks, enlargers, and strings of drying prints, all washed in deep red safelight. In the trays, prints are developing of photographs that have not yet been taken. Through the open door, the studio beyond shows the session still being prepared: a weathered adult male photographer holding a wooden large-format camera torwards an adult woman model standing behind a backlit translucent linen sheet, her nude silhouette softly outlined but entirely concealed by the fabric. In the darkroom, the finished portrait of that moment is already emerging in the developer, showing the exact pose she has not yet taken, her head turned and one hand lifting the edge of the sheet. A second print hanging to dry shows the photographer's face reacting to an image he has not yet seen. The paradox is consistent and restrained: every print is genuine silver-gelatin, with grain, tonal depth, and chemical stains, and each reveals a moment minutes ahead. A clock on the darkroom wall reads ten past four, while the clock in every developing print reads twenty past four. A tray of fixer holds a print of the empty studio after both have left. The darkroom timer, chemicals, and running water remain completely ordinary. The mood combines anticipation, intimacy, and a faint dread at seeing the future fixed in silver. Quiet photographic surrealism, meticulous darkroom detail, realistic wet paper and silver grain, deep safelight red, charcoal, silver, and warm skin tones. Dramatic red-and-shadow chiaroscuro with a slice of white studio light through the door, documentary composition, restrained sensuality, and large-format photographic realism.
A luxurious modernist house stands upon a remote coastal cliff, its monumental concrete walls interrupted by enormous panes of perfectly transparent glass. Inside, an elegant adult woman wearing a loosely draped black silk evening gown stands before a panoramic window overlooking a distant ocean. The window obeys a contradictory visual rule: objects directly behind its glass appear completely invisible, while objects normally concealed by walls become clearly visible through the same surface. The woman can see the ocean beyond the concrete wall but cannot see the garden located immediately outside the window. The resulting landscape appears geometrically coherent at first, yet careful examination reveals impossible discontinuities. A solitary white tree growing behind the wall is visible in full detail, while its branches disappear wherever they should be seen through the transparent glass. Several seabirds fly across the landscape, vanishing when they pass behind the windowpane and reappearing when they move behind the opaque concrete. The woman's reflection remains visible in the glass, but it appears superimposed upon a section of architecture that should be hidden. Her gown casts a perfectly ordinary shadow upon the floor, although portions of the shadow disappear beneath areas illuminated through the impossible window. Nearby, an elegant leather chair appears partially visible through the solid wall, its form interrupted only by a narrow transparent glass door. A small silver vase rests upon a table, but its reflection in the window reveals flowers that are entirely absent from the physical object. The woman studies the view with an expression of seductive curiosity and quiet apprehension. Minimalist architectural surrealism, sophisticated visual contradictions, restrained sensuality, exquisite concrete and glass textures, black, ivory, muted turquoise, and pale coastal gray. Naturalistic atmospheric lighting, rigorous perspective, powerful negative space, and haunting photographic realism.
